name: WSOS Baccalaureate Scholarship
deadline: 2027 cycle: application opens January 13, 2027; deadline February 25, 2027 at 9 p.m. PST (FAFSA or WASFA also due February 25, 2027); selection notification April 21, 2027
apply: Online WSOS application plus FAFSA or WASFA by the February deadline.
eligibility: Washington residents who have earned or will earn a Washington high school credential by June, with a cumulative GPA of at least 2.75 (or passing GED score), family income no higher than 125% of Washington median family income, planning an eligible STEM or health care major at a qualifying Washington institution. Undocumented applicants accepted.
notes: Selection considers financial need, commitment to STEM or health care, and academic achievement. Must enroll in at least three credits every fall, winter and spring term.

name: Golden LEAF Colleges and Universities Scholarship
value: High school seniors: up to $14,000 ($3,500 a year for up to 4 years)
deadline: 2027-28 cycle: applications open January 2027; application, transcript and FAFSA due March 1, 2027; awards announced May 2027
apply: Apply through the College Foundation of North Carolina (CFNC.org) portal and file the FAFSA.
eligibility: Graduating North Carolina high school seniors (or NC community college transfers) who are NC residents for tuition purposes, live in a qualifying rural, economically distressed NC county, have at least a 2.5 cumulative GPA and a Student Aid Index of $15,000 or less, and plan to attend a participating NC college or university full-time.
notes: Need-based eligibility cap (SAI 15,000 or less). Applicants should show commitment to returning to rural North Carolina after graduation.

provider: Texas FFA Association and Texas FFA Foundation
name: Texas FFA Scholarship Program
value: More than 140 scholarships a year, about $2.4 million annually in academic and award scholarships
deadline: Applications open January 1, 2027; area submission deadlines range from April 1 to April 19, 2027; state interviews June 4, 2027 at Tarleton State University
apply: Apply through your Texas FFA account on the roster system; finalists interview at the state level.
eligibility: Active Texas FFA members who are graduating seniors with a minimum 1000 SAT or 19 ACT (no superscores), who complete the FAFSA and meet GPA and major requirements in the program eligibility document.
notes: Selection based on academic and FFA achievements plus interview performance. Students receiving a Terry Foundation Scholarship are ineligible. The page still references the 2026-2027 FAFSA; confirm the correct FAFSA year.

name: Texas 4-H Foundation Scholarships (Baccalaureate, Technical, Courageous Heart)
value: Over $2.7 million in scholarships to over 230 Texas 4-H members each year
deadline: Application available November 1, 2026; deadline February 15, 2027 at 11:59 PM (no extensions); interviews April 23 to 25, 2027 in College Station; notifications May 2027
apply: Online application in the Texas 4-H scholarship portal with supplemental documents and school official or counselor verification; interviews in College Station.
eligibility: Active Texas 4-H members who are graduating seniors pursuing a bachelor's degree at an accredited Texas college or university (Baccalaureate), technical certification (Technical), or who have overcome extreme obstacles (Courageous Heart).
notes: Awards are based on academic record, 4-H experience and financial need.

provider: Georgia Foundation for Agriculture (Georgia Farm Bureau)
name: Scholarship for Agriculture (high school seniors)
value: 10 scholarships of $3,000; top 2 applicants eligible for an additional $1,500
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; applications reopen in November for the 2027 cycle. The 2026 deadline was March 1, 2026.
apply: Online application via the foundation's scholarship page (RegFox).
eligibility: Georgia residents who are graduating high school seniors, engaged in high school leadership, majoring in agriculture and environmental sciences, family and consumer sciences or a related agriculture field at a University System of Georgia institution, Berry College, Emmanuel College, or an accredited Georgia college with an agriculture program.
notes: Recipients must earn at least a 3.0 GPA in the first college semester.

provider: Iowa Economic Development Authority, Iowa Arts Council
name: Iowa Scholarship for the Arts
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline was April 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM, with finalist interviews on or about April 23, 2026.
apply: Online application; the review panel interviews the top-scoring applicants.
eligibility: Iowa residents graduating from an Iowa high school who have shown proven artistic ability in music, dance, visual arts, theatre, folklife or literature and are accepted as full-time undergraduates at an accredited Iowa college or university majoring in one of those areas.
notes: Family members or dependents of IEDA board members, Iowa Arts Council board members or IEDA staff are ineligible.

name: Florida Realtors Education Foundation Student Scholarship Program
value: Starting at $1,000; number and amounts vary each year ($226K awarded in 2026)
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; the 2026 application period is closed. Review is usually completed by the end of April.
apply: Online application only, with three reference letters (two from teachers or administrators on school letterhead).
eligibility: Florida residents (proof of legal Florida residency required) who are high school seniors attending an undergraduate college, or current undergraduate or graduate students. Out-of-state colleges allowed if the applicant intends to return to work in Florida. Any major; Realtors and their families may apply.
notes: Selection considers academic achievement, financial need, leadership, relationship to the Realtor family, and contributions to family, school and community. Real estate and related majors get priority consideration.

provider: Journalism Education Foundation of New England (New England Newspaper and Press Association)
name: New England Journalism Scholarship Program
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; scholarship applications are closed for 2026.
apply: Submit a cover letter, transcript, resume or biography, a letter of recommendation and at least three published or class-produced journalism pieces.
eligibility: High school seniors and undergraduates who live in Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island or Vermont, have a GPA of 3.0 or higher and study journalism or a related field.
notes: The MacGregor Fiske Award is also presented annually to an exceptional student journalist.

provider: Ohio News Media Foundation (Ohio News Media Association)
name: Ohio High School Journalism Scholarship
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline was Monday, May 25, 2026.
apply: Download and complete the PDF application from the Ohio News Media Association site.
eligibility: Graduating seniors at Ohio high schools with a minimum 2.5 (C+) GPA who plan to study journalism, advertising, marketing or communications at an accredited college or university.

name: NYFB Agricultural Youth Scholarship
value: District winners $250 each; state first place $3,000; state second place $2,000
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet announced; applications for 2026 scholarships have closed.
apply: Application through New York Farm Bureau; district winners advance to state selection.
eligibility: Graduating New York high school seniors planning agricultural careers (college or skilled trades) who live or work on a farm or are actively involved in agriculture and hold New York Farm Bureau membership (students can join free). Parental consent needed if under 18.

name: Michael P. Voiles Memorial Scholarship for Insurance and Agriculture
value: $3,000 annually per the MOFB scholarships page ($1,500 stipend paid directly to the institution); renewable up to three additional years
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 application period closed on March 31, 2026.
apply: Application form, teacher or counselor recommendation letter, resume, high school transcript and college acceptance notification.
eligibility: Missouri residents with current Missouri Farm Bureau membership (applicant, parent, grandparent or guardian) who are high school seniors accepted to a 4-year university with a declared major in insurance or agriculture (current undergraduates in those majors also eligible).
notes: Selection considers leadership in school and community. Renewal requires a 3.0 GPA, continued ag or insurance major and 12+ credit hours per semester.

name: INFB Ag Impact Scholarships
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; check back in January 2027. The 2026 deadline was March 1.
apply: Online application through the INFB state Scholarship Program (infb.org/scholarships).
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors planning agricultural careers with significant 4-H and/or FFA involvement and leadership experience, whose own or immediate family's Indiana Farm Bureau membership spans at least three consecutive years before applying.

name: Linda and Wayne Zaunbrecher Scholarship
value: Up to $3,000 per year (2026-27 amount; may vary); up to five awarded; renewable up to four consecutive years
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the page covers 2026 awards (made in May 2026) and lists no specific deadline date.
apply: Application through the foundation's portal; each parish Farm Bureau may submit one application.
eligibility: High school graduates whose applicant or parent is a current Louisiana Farm Bureau Federation member, with a minimum 2.5 cumulative high school GPA, majoring in agriculture, agricultural education, agribusiness, agriscience or a related field at an accredited Louisiana college or university.
notes: Renewal requires a 2.5 GPA, full-time enrollment and continued Farm Bureau membership.

name: Next Generation Hoosier Educators Scholarship
value: Up to $10,000 each year for four academic years (renewable)
deadline: 2027-2028 applications open October 1, 2026 and close February 27, 2027; decisions in April 2027
apply: Online application to the Indiana Commission for Higher Education.
eligibility: Indiana residents, U.S. citizens or eligible noncitizens, graduating from an accredited Indiana high school (or current college students), who meet one academic requirement: top 20% of graduating class, top 20% ACT or SAT score, or cumulative GPA of at least 3.0. Must attend an eligible Indiana institution full-time and pursue teaching licensure.
notes: Recipients must teach full-time for five years at an eligible Indiana school or repay a prorated amount.

provider: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development
name: A+ Scholarship Program
value: Reimburses the unpaid balance of tuition and general fees after federal aid; 2026-2027 cap $240 per credit hour or $8 per clock-hour
deadline: No single application deadline stated; FAFSA must be completed annually.
apply: Meet A+ requirements at a designated A+ high school, then file the FAFSA and enroll full-time at a participating school.
eligibility: U.S. citizens or permanent residents who attend a designated A+ high school for 2 years before graduation with at least 95% attendance in grades 9 to 12, an unweighted GPA of 2.5 or higher, 50 hours of unpaid tutoring or mentoring, good citizenship, and proficient or advanced Algebra I end-of-course score (alternative ACT/GPA pathways exist).
notes: Only for participating public community colleges or vocational/technical schools (and certain private two-year technical schools). Last-dollar award after federal aid. Eligibility ends 48 months after high school graduation or at associate degree.

provider: Florida Department of Education, Office of Student Financial Assistance
name: Benacquisto Scholarship Program
value: Institutional cost of attendance for an in-state student minus Bright Futures and the National Merit award
deadline: No application required; funding is automatic for eligible National Merit Scholars who enroll at a participating institution. 2027-28 fact sheet not yet posted.
apply: No formal application; become a National Merit Scholar and enroll at an eligible Florida institution that is a college sponsor.
eligibility: Florida residents who earn a standard Florida high school diploma, are National Merit Scholars, and enroll at an eligible Florida postsecondary institution in the fall term after graduation.
notes: 2026-27 fact sheet lists only nine participating Florida institutions (including UF, FSU and University of Miami). Renewal requires a 3.0 cumulative GPA. Related college-specific FSU Benacquisto record exists.

provider: Florida Department of Education, Office of Student Financial Assistance
name: Florida Bright Futures: Gold Seal Vocational Scholars (GSV)
value: Per-credit-hour or clock-hour award for career and technical programs (amount set annually; not stated on the fact sheet)
deadline: Submit the Florida Financial Aid Application (FFAA) no later than August 31 after high school graduation
apply: Submit the Florida Financial Aid Application (FFAA).
eligibility: Florida residents, U.S. citizens or eligible noncitizens, with a weighted 3.0 GPA in non-elective high school courses, a 3.5 unweighted GPA in at least three full Career and Technical Education credits, minimum test scores (ACT Reading 19, English 17, Math 19; or SAT EBRW 490, Math 480; or PERT), and 30 volunteer hours, 100 paid work hours or a 100-hour combination (75 volunteer hours for students entering grade 9 in 2024-25 or later).
notes: Usable only for applied technology diploma, technical degree (AAS or AS) or career certificate programs, not AA or bachelor's degrees. A parallel Gold Seal CAPE Scholars award is based on CAPE industry certifications.

provider: New York State Higher Education Services Corporation (HESC)
name: NYS STEM Incentive Program
value: Covers tuition at a SUNY or CUNY college (up to SUNY resident undergraduate tuition), 4 years for a bachelor's degree or 2 years for an associate degree
deadline: HESC states the program is currently closed; no 2027 application dates posted.
apply: Application through HESC when the program is open.
eligibility: Graduates of a New York State high school ranked in the top 10 percent of their graduating class, U.S. citizens or eligible noncitizens and legal New York residents for 12 continuous months, who pursue an approved STEM degree at a SUNY or CUNY college starting the fall after graduation.
notes: Must agree to live in New York State and work in an approved STEM occupation for five years, or the award converts to a loan. Page says the program is currently closed; confirm it reopens before listing as live.
